questions.question: What extra behaviour does @RestControllerAdvice add to @ControllerAdvice?
options: It writes handler return values to the response body, as @ResponseBody does
It makes handlers run on a separate thread
It applies only to GET requests
questions.explanation: @RestControllerAdvice is @ControllerAdvice plus @ResponseBody, so handler results are sent as JSON.

questions.question: Handlers exist for OutOfStockException and for Exception. An OutOfStockException is thrown. Which handler runs?
questions.explanation: Spring picks the most specific handler for the thrown type, so the OutOfStockException handler wins.

questions.question: In the pharmacy app, a client tries to sell 5 cough syrups when 3 are left. The handler returns 409 with the exception message. Which body does the client see?
questions.explanation: The OutOfStockException handler builds an ApiMessage with status 409 and the exception's own message.

questions.question: The pharmacy app has a catch-all Exception handler returning 500 and no handler for type mismatch. What does GET /medicines/abc return when the id is a long?
questions.explanation: The type mismatch exception matches the catch-all Exception handler, so the client mistake becomes a 500 reply.

questions.question: A developer writes a catch-all handler that returns ex.getMessage() to the client and does not log the exception. What are the two problems?
options: It runs too slowly and uses more memory
It may leak internal details, and the real error is lost from the server log
It changes every status to 200 and disables validation
It stops other handlers from being registered
questions.explanation: Raw messages can reveal internals to strangers, and without logging nobody can investigate the failure later.
